Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. DMS: Database Migration Service; MSK: Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka; SFTP: Secure File Transfer Protocol; ETL: extract, transform, load; CTAS: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT; ECS: Elastic Container Service; LLM: large language model; DAG: directed acyclic graph; MWAA: Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow; SNS: Simple Notification Service; SQS: Simple Queue Service; RDS: Relational Database Service; BI: business intelligence; LF: Lake Formation; PII: personally identifiable information; IVF: inverted file; SSE: server-side encryption; IAM: Identity and Access Management; RBAC: role-based access control; TBAC: tag-based access control; ABAC: attribute-based access control; PITR: point-in-time recovery; TTL: time to live; DPU: data processing unit; DB: database; DLQ: dead-letter queue; DQ: data quality; TLS: Transport Layer Security

  • See the whole data platform on one page
  • Use the service choosers to turn a requirement into a service
  • Review the look-alike services that the exam uses as distractors
  • Recall the numbers and rules worth memorizing

2The Whole Pipeline on One Page

Running case

Kestrel Freight, Start to Finish

  • Ingest truck telemetry (streams) and order files (batch)
  • Store raw data in S3, serving data in Redshift and DynamoDB
  • Catalog it, transform it, orchestrate it, monitor it
  • Secure and govern every step
  • Your job: recall which service owns which step

3Service Chooser by Requirement

Exam tip

Read the requirement word first (cost, overhead, latency, security, near real time), then pick the service from the chooser that owns that word.

Ingestion

Requirement Service
SaaS data (Salesforce, Zendesk, SAP) into S3 or Redshift, no code Amazon AppFlow
Database copy or ongoing replication (CDC) AWS DMS
Custom, replayable stream, many consumers, per-key order Kinesis Data Streams
Load a stream into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch with no code Amazon Data Firehose
Existing Kafka workloads Amazon MSK
Table change feed from DynamoDB DynamoDB Streams
SFTP partners into S3 AWS Transfer Family
On-premises file shares into AWS AWS DataSync
Offline bulk transfer AWS Snow Family
Third-party datasets AWS Data Exchange
Start on arrival of a file S3 Event Notifications / EventBridge
Start on a time EventBridge Scheduler, Glue scheduled trigger

Transform and process

Requirement Service
Serverless Spark ETL with a catalog AWS Glue
Control of Hadoop and Spark versions, very large clusters Amazon EMR (Serverless for no cluster)
Small event-driven transformation AWS Lambda
SQL transformations in the warehouse Redshift (ELT)
SQL ETL on S3 Athena CTAS and INSERT INTO
Visual, no-code preparation AWS Glue DataBrew
Stateful stream processing Managed Service for Apache Flink
Containers for custom code ECS or EKS (Fargate), AWS Batch for many jobs
LLM processing of text at scale Bedrock batch inference

Orchestrate and automate

Requirement Service
Serverless multi-service workflow with retries, branches, approval Step Functions
Existing Airflow DAGs Amazon MWAA
Glue-only chain Glue workflows
Route events and schedule EventBridge (bus, Pipes, Scheduler)
Alerts and fan-out SNS; buffer with SQS

Store

Requirement Service
Data lake, any format, cheap Amazon S3 (Parquet; S3 Tables / Iceberg for tables)
Analytics warehouse Amazon Redshift
Key lookups at scale, single-digit ms Amazon DynamoDB
Relational transactions RDS / Aurora
Durable in-memory, microsecond reads Amazon MemoryDB
Graph Amazon Neptune
Search, logs, vectors Amazon OpenSearch Service
Vector search in PostgreSQL Aurora PostgreSQL + pgvector (HNSW)

Catalog, quality, analysis

Requirement Service
Technical catalog shared by engines Glue Data Catalog (+ crawlers)
Business catalog, glossary, subscriptions SageMaker Catalog
Data quality rules Glue Data Quality (DQDL), DataBrew rulesets
SQL on S3 Amazon Athena
BI dashboards QuickSight (Amazon Quick)
Operational time series Managed Grafana

Operate, secure, govern

Requirement Service
Metrics and alarms CloudWatch
Who called the API CloudTrail (data events for objects), CloudTrail Lake
Configuration history and compliance AWS Config
Credentials with rotation Secrets Manager
Keys AWS KMS (customer managed for control and sharing)
Central lake permissions Lake Formation (LF-tags, filters)
Find PII in S3 Amazon Macie
Central backups AWS Backup
Region restrictions SCPs (aws:RequestedRegion)

4Look-Alike Services: How to Tell Them Apart

Exam tip

When two look-alikes both seem to work, the question names the difference: replay, serverless, no code, existing Kafka or Airflow, or who made the call.

Pair Difference
Kinesis Data Streams vs Data Firehose Streams: you build consumers, replay, ordering by key. Firehose: delivers to a destination, no replay.
Kinesis vs MSK AWS-native shards vs Apache Kafka; MSK for existing Kafka
Glue vs EMR Glue: serverless ETL, catalog. EMR: control, ecosystem, huge scale.
Glue vs Lambda Glue: large Spark jobs. Lambda: small, 15-minute, event-driven.
Athena vs Redshift Athena: serverless SQL on S3, pay per data scanned. Redshift: warehouse for heavy, repeated, concurrent analytics.
Redshift Spectrum vs federated query Spectrum: files in S3. Federated: live RDS/Aurora.
Step Functions vs MWAA Serverless state machines vs managed Airflow DAGs
Glue workflows vs Step Functions Glue-only vs any AWS service
SNS vs SQS Publish/subscribe push vs queue pull
EventBridge bus vs Pipes Many-to-many routing vs point-to-point with filter and enrichment
DynamoDB vs RDS Key-based, schemaless, scales out vs joins and transactions
DynamoDB vs MemoryDB Serverless key-value store vs durable in-memory, microsecond reads
HNSW vs IVF Graph index, high recall, more memory vs clusters, faster build, less memory
Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store Rotation, per-secret charge vs configuration, free standard tier
SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS Default, no key control vs your key, audit, sharing
IAM role vs user Temporary credentials for workloads vs long-term credentials
RBAC vs TBAC vs ABAC By role vs by resource tag vs compare principal and resource attributes
CloudWatch vs CloudTrail vs Config Metrics and logs vs API calls (who) vs resource configuration history
Glue Data Catalog vs SageMaker Catalog Technical vs business catalog
DataBrew vs Glue Data Quality Visual rules for analysts vs DQDL rules for engineers

5Numbers and Rules Worth RememberingVerify live

Area Fact
Exam 65 questions (50 scored), 130 minutes, 720 of 1,000, domains 34 / 26 / 22 / 18
Kinesis Data Streams Shard write 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s, read 2 MB/s shared; retention 24 hours to 365 days; enhanced fan-out consumers 20
Firehose S3 buffer default 5 MiB or 300 s (interval 0–900 s)
DynamoDB Item 400 KB; PITR 35 days; TTL deletes within a few days
Lambda 15 min; 128–10,240 MB; /tmp 512–10,240 MB; default 1,000 concurrency
API Gateway 10,000 rps default, 5,000 burst
Step Functions Standard: 1 year, exactly once; Express: 5 min, at least once
S3 lifecycle < 128 KB not transitioned by default; minimum durations 30 / 90 / 180 days
Redshift COPY from many files (multiple of slices); KEY/ALL/EVEN/AUTO; Data API results 24 h
Glue DPU = 4 vCPU + 16 GB; retries 0–10; bookmarks default disabled; trigger starts 2 crawlers
KMS Rotation 365 days (customer managed), deletion wait 7–30 days; AWS managed keys cannot be shared
CloudTrail Event history 90 days; data events off by default; Lake closed to new customers from 31 May 2026
Exam tip

Memorize the shapes of the limits (which service has which kind of limit) before the exact numbers, and check the AWS page for any number tagged Verify live.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Method Read the requirement word (cost, overhead, latency, security, near real time), match the service, eliminate look-alikes
Ingestion SaaS AppFlow; DB DMS; stream Kinesis/MSK/Firehose; SFTP Transfer Family; incremental bookmarks/CDC
Transformation Glue (serverless), EMR (control), Lambda (small), Athena CTAS; Parquet + partition + compact
Orchestration Step Functions (serverless), MWAA (Airflow), Glue workflows, EventBridge; retry, DLQ, idempotent
Stores S3, Redshift, DynamoDB, RDS/Aurora, MemoryDB, Neptune, OpenSearch; Iceberg; HNSW/IVF
Catalog and lifecycle Glue Data Catalog + crawlers; lifecycle rules, versioning, TTL, UNLOAD; AWS Backup
Operations CloudWatch metrics/logs/alarms → SNS; CloudTrail who; Config what changed; Glue DQ / DataBrew quality
Security Roles not keys, Secrets Manager, Lake Formation, KMS, TLS, Macie, SCP Regions, mask or anonymize
